To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have shown that, by using the first model for dipole scattering amplitude in momentum space [10] with the fluctuations included, we have been able to reproduce the latest HERA data for the F2 structure function, specially in the charm quark region, by using a BK-inspired parametrization for this amplitude.

the dipole model in momentum space, with the inclusion of the fluctuation effects in the BK equation, can be used to describe the latest HERA data, with the inclusion in the dipole model of the charm quark effects, and that the fluctuations are not expected to strongly influence the scattering at HERA energies.

the BK equation with fluctuations, when solved in coordinate space, can describe HERA data, specially with a charm mass included in the scattering amplitude; the BK equation in momentum space with fluctuations, when applied to HERA data, can be used to extract the strong coupling constant, and the fluctuations can be included in the dipole-proto cross section in momentum space, and the results can be compared to the HERA measurements.
